items.explanation: A + el always joins into al: voy al cine.
optionNotes: A and el always join into al.
Del is de + el (of / from the).

items.explanation: De + el always joins into del: el coche del profesor.
optionNotes: De and el always join into del.

items.prompt: ___ agua de aquí es muy buena.
items.explanation: Agua is feminine, but it starts with a stressed a-, so the singular article is el: el agua.
optionNotes: A feminine noun with a stressed a- takes el in the singular.
Un means “a”; the sentence is about the water here.

items.prompt: You meet Mr. Ruiz at work. You say: “___”
items.explanation: When you speak to someone directly, the title has no article: Buenos días, señor Ruiz.
optionNotes: No article when you speak directly to the person.
The title comes before the name.
Un is never used with a title.
